rounds.proof_sketch: Fixed input shape [16, 16384] yields size = 16 * 16384 = 262144 elements. Original condition: 262144 >= 4096 && 262144 % 4 == 0 → TRUE. Mutant condition: 262144 >= 4097 && 262144 % 4 == 0 → TRUE. Both conditions evaluate to TRUE, so both versions execute the identical vectorized kernel path.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the threshold for selecting the vectorized kernel from 4096 to 4097 elements. However, the fixed input shape of [16, 16384] produces exactly 262144 elements, which is far above both thresholds. Consequently, both the original (size >= 4096) and mutant (size >= 4097) conditions evaluate to TRUE, causing both to execute the exact same elu_kernel_vectorized4 kernel. Since the same kernel is executed with the same parameters, the outputs are numerically identical regardless of input values. The only way to trigger a difference would require an input tensor with exactly 4096 elements, which would violate the fixed-shape contract.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed-shape contract. The mutation only affects kernel selection for tensors with size in [4096, 4096], but the fixed input size of 262144 far exceeds this range, causing both versions to take identical code paths.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing kernel dispatch thresholds, ensure test configurations include tensor sizes that straddle the threshold boundaries. For this kernel, testing with shapes yielding exactly 4096 elements (e.g., [64, 64] or [1, 4096]) would expose differences in dispatch behavior. Consider adding boundary-value tests at kernel selection thresholds to future test suites.
